title: Fix typos and unclear sentences in the Session 1 notes
body:
## Problem
The Session 1 notes may contain typos or sentences that a first-year student finds confusing.

## Context
Beginners judge the whole repo by Session 1.

## Expected outcome
A clearer `sessions/session-01/README.md` and `lesson.py` comments.

## Relevant files
`sessions/session-01/README.md`, `sessions/session-01/lesson.py`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] At least three improvements
- [ ] `python start.py test` still passes

## Difficulty
beginner

title: Add a colour-blind-safe palette and line styles to the live apps
body:
## Problem
The apps use red and blue curves for the as-built room and your design, and red for 'no shade'; some colour-blind users cannot tell them apart.

## Context
Accessibility is part of the quality checklist (QUALITY.md, item 9).

## Expected outcome
A palette plus dashed or dotted line styles that stay distinguishable in light and dark mode.

## Relevant files
`sessions/session-01/app.html`, `sessions/session-02/app.html`, `sessions/session-03/app.html`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All curves distinguishable in grayscale
- [ ] Screenshot added to the pull request

## Difficulty
beginner

title: Session 2 app: draw the sun path for the whole day on a sky dome
body:
## Problem
The Session 2 app shows the sun at one hour only; students cannot see the whole path across the sky, or why the sun is in the north at noon in a Chennai summer.

## Context
Sun-path diagrams are the everyday tool architects use to plan shading.

## Expected outcome
A new graph in `sessions/session-02/app.html`: a polar sun-path diagram (altitude as rings, azimuth round the circle) for the chosen day, with the current hour marked and the window's facing direction drawn.

## Relevant files
`sessions/session-02/app.html`, `sessions/session-02/lesson.py`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] On day 172 the noon point is north of the zenith for latitude 13.08 N
- [ ] Works in light and dark mode and at phone width

## Difficulty
intermediate

title: Add Session 4: a roof that stores heat
body:
## Problem
The roadmap's first milestone does not exist yet.

## Context
See `promo/roadmap.md`, Session 4. On a top floor the roof is the largest heat source, and the shipped model gives it no heat storage, so roof heat reaches the room instantly.

## Expected outcome
`sessions/session-04/` with README (sections A to F), lesson, checkpoint, exercises and app in the same style as Sessions 1 to 3.

## Relevant files
`promo/roadmap.md`, `sessions/session-03/lesson.py`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Checkpoint prints PASS and the roadmap checkpoint is met
- [ ] Added to the tests

## Difficulty
intermediate

title: Add Session 5: fins, jaalis and sunlit walls
body:
## Problem
Session 2 has only horizontal overhangs, which cannot block the low west sun, and Session 3 treats the walls as shaded.

## Context
Roadmap Session 5. Jaali screens are a traditional Indian answer to low sun that still let air through.

## Expected outcome
A lesson and app where fin depth, fin spacing and jaali open area are sliders, with the shaded fraction and the resulting room temperature.

## Relevant files
`sessions/session-02/lesson.py`, `sessions/session-03/lesson.py`, `promo/roadmap.md`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The roadmap checkpoint is met and shown in a figure
- [ ] Checkpoint added

## Difficulty
intermediate

title: Reproduce the Target: a passive-design tool for the Chennai room
body:
## Problem
The Target describes a full passive-design tool (layered roof, sunlit walls, fins and jaalis, fan and humidity comfort, a month of weather); there is no public implementation.

## Context
The Target figure comes from Session 3; the extended tool is private on purpose. The roadmap gives the path.

## Expected outcome
Your own implementation, written from the roadmap, plus a figure like the Target for a whole month.

## Relevant files
`promo/roadmap.md`, `sessions/session-03/lesson.py`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] With the shipped settings your tool reproduces the Session 3 peaks (46.3, 40.2, 37.7, 36.0 and 36.9 C) within 0.1 K
- [ ] Short write-up of your method and the design you recommend

## Difficulty
advanced

title: Translate the Session 1 notes into Hindi
body:
## Problem
Students who prefer Hindi cannot read Session 1 comfortably.

## Context
This project teaches first- and second-year students across India; translations widen who can join.

## Expected outcome
`sessions/session-01/README.hi.md` with a faithful Hindi translation of sections A to F, linked from the main README.

## Relevant files
`sessions/session-01/README.md`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] All sections translated
- [ ] Equations, code blocks and file names unchanged
- [ ] Link added to the main README

## Difficulty
beginner
